item.title: Trump Postpones Iran Power Plant Threat as Hormuz Crisis Hangs in Balance
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday he had given orders to postpone any military strikes against Iranian power plants for five days, hours ahead of a deadline that threatened further escalation in the conflict now in its fourth week.

item.title: Trump Administration Reimburses TotalEnergies $928M to Scrap Offshore Wind Leases, Pivot to LNG
item.description: The Trump administration has struck a $928 million deal with TotalEnergies to abandon two major U.S. offshore wind leases and redirect the capital into LNG and oil and gas development, marking a decisive shift in strategy after federal courts blocked efforts to halt projects on national security grounds.

item.title: Oil Prices Have Not Climbed Enough to Cause Demand Destruction, US Energy Secretary Says
item.description: Global oil prices have not climbed enough to cause demand destruction, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Monday at the CERAWeek energy conference in Houston, Texas, even as markets continued to gyrate and global oil prices remained near $100 a barrel due to the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: Trump Delays Iran Energy Strikes as Confusion Swirls Over ‘Productive’ Talks
item.description: President Donald Trump said the US would postpone strikes against Iran’s energy infrastructure after what he called “productive conversations” with the country, in comments that spurred confusion over the participants in the talks and parameters of a deal.

item.title: Bahrain Pushes UN Vote to Authorize Force in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Bahrain has put forward a draft United Nations Security Council resolution that would authorize countries to use "all necessary means" - diplomatic language for force - to protect commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, according to a text seen by Reuters on Monday.

item.title: Regulators Push Back on Shipping Surcharges as Hormuz Disruption Ripples Globally
item.description: Indian shipping regulators and related authorities seem to be keeping a close watch on ongoing supply chain dynamics for export trades as ocean carriers arguably tend to profiteer from capacity disruption, especially in a larger crisis situation.
